pages.title: Colony-keepers
pages.text:
The Colony-keepers tended hives that hummed in the Loom's own key, and March flowers that hummed back.\
They did not own their colonies. They were on good terms with them. That is the whole of the method.

pages.title: Continue
pages.text:
Before the Cut that conversation ran at continent scale: hives in the Loom's key, flowers humming back across hanging fields.\
What they lost was the large talk.\
A great many hives went quiet rather than angry.\
Quiet is a kind of loyalty.

pages.title: Continue
pages.text: There are no bees in the void until you make somewhere a bee wants to be.

pages.title: Swarm Strand
pages.text:
*You do not own a hive. You are on good terms with it.*\
Seated. The Colony-keepers answer when this Post hums.

pages.title: Their camp
pages.text: The Colony-keepers keep a camp in the March steppe: huts, a fire, a Tribe Hearth, a Air totem, a banner and four Kin — an Elder, a Drummer, a Hunter and a Weaver.

pages.title: Continue
pages.text: Their hearth favours honey, flowers, Lantern Down. Their Elder trades hives and March flowers, and at Voice standing presses the tribe's Mark into your hand.
